title: Improve SDK error context and surface actionable recovery guidance across Python/TS/Go
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a consistent, actionable error surface across Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) that includes enriched context for telemetry and human operators, plus user-facing recovery guidance that helps application developers decide whether to retry, back off, or surface an alternative UX.

Background: Current SDKs diverge in how they represent transient vs terminal failures, what context fields they include (request_id, model, token counts, server_retry_after), and how they expose streaming interruption reasons. That makes cross-service debugging and automatic retry policies brittle.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Each SDK exports a stable Error object/class with these canonical string fields: code, message, request_id, model, node_region, server_retry_after (ISO8601 or seconds), is_idempotent_hint ("true"/"false"), tokens_consumed (string int), and reference (link to docs).
- Error codes mapped to a small canonical set (e.g., INVALID_ARGUMENT, RATE_LIMIT, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, TIMEOUT, INTERNAL, STREAM_INTERRUPTED, CONNECTION_RESET).
- SDKs surface a machine-friendly retryable hint ("retryable"/"non-retryable"/"conditional") and a short actionable message intended for developer consoles (<=140 chars).
- Streaming APIs return a resumable error shape when applicable with resume_token and last_valid_offset fields (as strings).
- Comprehensive cross-language tests and sample snippets (Python/TS/Go) demonstrating backoff, idempotency key usage, and stream resume flow.

Design notes:
- Keep the public surface minimal: we expose a typed Error class and helper utilities (should_retry(error), suggested_backoff(error)). SDKs may include additional per-language diagnostic wrappers.
- For legacy compatibility, map existing exception types to the new canonical codes and keep a migration guide.
- Telemetry: errors MUST include request_id and model to correlate with server logs and console traces.
- Security: avoid logging PII in error messages; include a short fingerprint if necessary.

Non-goals: Changing server-side error semantics (server teams will publish mapping guidance separately). This ticket focuses on client-side shaping and examples.
tasks: Define canonical error code set and field definitions (spec doc)
Implement Python Error class + should_retry/suggested_backoff helpers
Implement TypeScript error types and runtime assertion helpers
Implement Go error wrappers compatible with idiomatic error handling
Add stream-resume protocol: resume_token + last_offset semantics
Add cross-language unit/integration tests and fuzz tests for deserialization
Write migration guide and quickstart snippets for console/docs
Add feature flag in SDKs to toggle old vs new error surface for rollout
